plain.text: Should we keep on sinning so that grace may increase? By no means! We died to sin; how can we live in it any longer? All of us who were baptised into Christ Jesus were baptised into his death. We were buried with him through baptism into death, so that, just as Christ was raised from the dead, we too may live a new life. Our old self was crucified with him, so that we would no longer be slaves to sin. Count yourselves dead to sin but alive to God in Christ Jesus. Do not let sin rule your bodies. Offer yourselves to God, because sin shall no longer be your master, for you are not under law, but under grace.

Does that mean we may sin because we are under grace? By no means! Whatever you give yourself to obey, you become its slave, either to sin, which leads to death, or to obedience, which leads to righteousness. Thanks be to God that you obeyed from the heart and have been set free from sin. Now offer yourselves to righteousness, leading to holiness. "For the wages of sin is death, but the gift of God is eternal life in Christ Jesus our Lord."

summary.bigIdea: Grace is not an excuse to keep sinning; united with Christ, we are free to live a new life for God.
points: Baptised into Christ, believers share in his death and his new life.
Count yourselves dead to sin and alive to God.
"The wages of sin is death, but the gift of God is eternal life."
summary.reflection: Paul says we become slaves to what we obey. What do you find yourself most often serving?
